Table: pH levels of common substances:
Substance: Lemon juice | Vinegar | Milk | Baking soda solution | Soap | Bleach
pH: 2.3 | 2.9 | 6.6 | 8.3 | 10.0 | 12.6
Based on the table, which substance is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: The lower the pH, the stronger the acid. Lemon juice has the lowest pH (2.3) among the options, making it the strongest acid. Bleach (12.6) is a strong base.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem: A graph shows the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b. Chlorophyll a shows peak absorption at wavelengths of approximately 430 nm and 662 nm. Chlorophyll b shows peak absorption at approximately 453 nm and 642 nm. What can be concluded based on the absorption spectra?
options: The two chlorophyll types absorb light at exactly the same wavelengths
Both chlorophyll types absorb strongly in the blue-violet and red regions, but their peak wavelengths differ slightly
Chlorophyll a absorbs only green light
Chlorophyll b does not absorb red light
questions.explanation: Both forms have peak absorption in blue-violet (~430-453 nm) and red (~642-662 nm) regions, but the exact peak wavelengths differ, reflecting their slightly different molecular structures.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Rate of photosynthesis (μmol CO₂/m²/s) at different light intensities (μmol photons/m²/s) and CO₂ concentrations:
Light intensity: 0 | 100 | 200 | 400 | 600 | 800
Rate at 350 ppm CO₂: 0 | 5 | 12 | 22 | 28 | 28
Rate at 700 ppm CO₂: 0 | 5 | 14 | 28 | 38 | 42
At 800 μmol photons/m²/s, what is the effect of increasing CO₂ from 350 ppm to 700 ppm on the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: At 800 light intensity, the rate goes from 28 (at 350 ppm CO₂) to 42 (at 700 ppm CO₂), showing a substantial increase of 14 units.

questions.stem: A scientist wants to test whether a new fertilizer increases plant growth. She plants 50 seeds in soil with the new fertilizer and another 50 seeds in soil without fertilizer. After four weeks, she measures the height of all plants. In this experiment, what is the control group?
options: The seeds that did not germinate
questions.explanation: The control group is the one that does not receive the treatment (no fertilizer), providing a baseline for comparison against the experimental group (with fertilizer).

questions.stem: A researcher studying the effect of temperature on enzyme activity sets up five test tubes with the same enzyme and substrate solution. Tube 1 is kept at 10°C, Tube 2 at 20°C, Tube 3 at 30°C, Tube 4 at 40°C, and Tube 5 at 50°C. The rate of product formation is measured in each tube. What is the independent variable in this experiment?
options: The volume of solution in each tube
questions.explanation: The independent variable is what the researcher manipulates — temperature. The dependent variable (what is measured) is the rate of product formation.

questions.stem: A team of researchers wants to determine whether a new drug reduces blood pressure. They give the drug to 100 patients and a placebo to another 100 patients. Neither the patients nor the doctors administering the treatment know which group receives the actual drug. What is this type of experimental design called?
questions.explanation: In a double-blind study, neither the participants nor the researchers administering the treatment know who receives the actual treatment versus the placebo. This prevents bias.

questions.stem: Experiment: A student tests the effect of different wavelengths of light on the rate of photosynthesis in spinach leaves. She places leaf discs in a sodium bicarbonate solution and measures the time it takes for the discs to float (indicating oxygen production). She uses red, blue, green, and white light. Why should the student also include a dark condition (no light) in her experiment?
options: To provide a positive control showing maximum photosynthesis
To provide a negative control showing that no light produces no photosynthesis
To test whether spinach can photosynthesize in the dark
To save time by running more conditions at once
questions.explanation: The dark condition is the negative control: it shows that in the absence of light, no oxygen is produced, confirming that any oxygen production in the light conditions is due to photosynthesis and not other factors.

questions.stem: A scientist tests the effect of soil salinity on bean plant growth. She plants identical bean seeds in three groups of pots: Group A receives fresh water, Group B receives water with 1% salt, and Group C receives water with 3% salt. All other conditions (light, temperature, soil type) are kept identical. After six weeks, she measures the average plant height in each group. Which variable is the dependent variable?
options: The salt concentration of the water
The average plant height after six weeks
The type of bean seed used
The amount of light the plants receive
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is what is measured as the outcome of the experiment — the average plant height. The salt concentration is the independent variable that is manipulated.

questions.stem: A research team wants to test whether a new fertilizer increases crop yield. They have limited land, so they test the fertilizer on 10 plots and use 10 identical plots without fertilizer as controls. The plots are randomly assigned to the two groups. Why is random assignment important in this experiment?
options: It guarantees the fertilizer will work
It helps ensure that the two groups are similar, reducing the influence of confounding variables like soil quality differences
It makes the results easier to calculate
It eliminates the need for a control group
questions.explanation: Random assignment distributes unknown differences (soil quality, drainage, etc.) roughly evenly between groups, so any yield difference can be more confidently attributed to the fertilizer rather than pre-existing plot differences.

questions.stem: Two scientists disagree about the cause of the extinction of the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. Scientist 1 argues that a large asteroid impact in the Yucatán Peninsula caused a global dust cloud that blocked sunlight and disrupted the food chain. Scientist 2 argues that massive volcanic eruptions in the Deccan Traps of India released enough gas and ash to cause climate change that killed the dinosaurs. Which piece of evidence would best support Scientist 1's view?
options: The discovery of an iridium layer (an element rare on Earth but common in asteroids) at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary worldwide
Evidence that volcanoes in the Deccan Traps erupted for thousands of years
Fossil evidence that dinosaurs existed for 165 million years
The existence of other extinction events in Earth's history
questions.explanation: A global iridium layer is key evidence for an asteroid impact because iridium is abundant in asteroids but extremely rare in Earth's crust. This directly supports the impact hypothesis of Scientist 1.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Boiling points of four substances at standard pressure:
Substance: Water | Ethanol | Mercury | Acetic acid
Boiling point (°C): 100 | 78 | 357 | 118
Based on the table, which substance would boil first if a mixture of all four was heated gradually?
questions.explanation: The substance with the lowest boiling point boils first. Ethanol at 78°C has the lowest boiling point of the four substances listed.

questions.stem: A student wants to test how the angle of a ramp affects the distance a toy car travels after rolling off the ramp. She tests the car at ramp angles of 10°, 20°, 30°, and 40°. Which of the following should she keep constant to ensure a fair test?
options: The type of toy car and the height at the top of the ramp
The surface the car lands on, which may change between trials
questions.explanation: To ensure a fair test, all variables except the ramp angle must be kept constant: the same car, same starting height, and same landing surface. The angle is the independent variable being changed.

questions.stem: A biologist is studying whether a certain species of fish prefers water with high oxygen levels. She observes fish in three different ponds: one with an oxygen pump, one with heavy algae growth, and one with no special features. She counts fish in each pond over a week. A weakness of this observational study compared to a controlled experiment is that:
options: There is no control over other differences between the ponds that could affect fish preference
Fish cannot be observed in their natural habitat
The study takes too long to produce results
questions.explanation: In an observational study, the researcher does not control the conditions. The ponds differ in multiple ways (algae, aeration, size, depth), so any difference in fish counts could be due to factors other than oxygen level.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem: A researcher plots the growth of two plant species over 60 days. Species A grows from 2 cm to 30 cm in a pattern that curves steeply upward. Species B grows from 2 cm to 18 cm in a roughly straight line. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Species B grows faster than Species A overall
Species A shows accelerating (exponential-like) growth while Species B grows at a more constant rate
Both species grow at exactly the same rate
Species B will eventually exceed Species A in height
questions.explanation: The steep upward curve of Species A indicates accelerating growth (increasing rate over time), while the straight line of Species B indicates constant-rate growth. The data do not support the other conclusions.

questions.stem: Researchers investigate the effect of a new antibiotic on bacteria. They grow bacteria in five identical dishes. Dish 1 receives 0 mg of antibiotic (control). Dishes 2-5 receive 5, 10, 20, and 40 mg respectively. After 24 hours, they measure the number of live bacteria in each dish. The results show fewer bacteria surviving as antibiotic dose increases. What is the most reasonable conclusion?
options: Higher doses of the antibiotic kill more bacteria
The bacteria grew faster with the antibiotic
The dose of antibiotic has no effect on bacteria
questions.explanation: The dose-response relationship (fewer survivors at higher doses) supports the conclusion that higher antibiotic doses are more effective at killing bacteria. The control dish confirms the baseline.

questions.stem: Two geologists study a rock layer containing fossils of marine organisms found high in the Himalayan mountains. Geologist 1 claims the fossils prove the area was once under the ocean, and the rocks were pushed upward when the Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate. Geologist 2 claims the fossils were carried to the mountains by glaciers or transported by rivers. Which observation would most strongly support Geologist 1's claim?
options: The fossils are found in marine sedimentary rock layers that are undisturbed and continuous along the mountain range
The fossils show signs of being broken and worn as if transported
The fossils are found only in loose surface deposits
The fossils are from species that also live in freshwater lakes
questions.explanation: Undisturbed, continuous marine sedimentary layers high in the mountains support the claim that the area was once seafloor that was uplifted. Broken/worn or loose deposits would support transport (Geologist 2's view).

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Number of daylight hours in a northern city by month:
Month: Jan | Mar | May | Jul | Sep | Nov
Daylight (hours): 9 | 12 | 15 | 16 | 12 | 9
Based on the table, which two months have the same amount of daylight?
questions.explanation: March and September both have 12 hours of daylight. These are the equinoxes, when day and night are nearly equal in length.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Average heart rate (beats per minute) of mammals at different body masses:
Animal: Mouse | Rabbit | Cat | Human | Elephant
Mass (kg): 0.03 | 2 | 4 | 70 | 5,000
Heart rate (bpm): 600 | 205 | 190 | 72 | 30
What general trend does the table show?
options: Larger animals have faster heart rates
Smaller animals have faster heart rates
Heart rate is the same for all mammals
There is no relationship between mass and heart rate
questions.explanation: The table shows an inverse relationship: the smallest animal (mouse, 0.03 kg) has the fastest heart rate (600 bpm), and the largest (elephant) has the slowest (30 bpm).

questions.stem: A nutrition scientist wants to determine whether a high-protein diet increases muscle mass in athletes. She recruits 200 athletes and randomly assigns half to a high-protein diet and half to a standard diet for 12 weeks. Both groups follow the same training program. At the end, she measures muscle mass in both groups. Why is it important that both groups follow the same training program?
options: Training is the independent variable in this study
Training is a confounding variable that could affect muscle mass independently of diet
Training prevents the athletes from gaining muscle
The training program has no effect on the outcome
questions.explanation: Training is a confounding variable because it independently affects muscle mass. By keeping training identical for both groups, any difference in muscle mass can be attributed to the diet rather than training.

questions.stem: Two biologists debate why a population of finches on an island developed larger beaks over several decades. Biologist 1 argues that during a drought, only large seeds were available, and finches with larger beaks survived and reproduced more (natural selection). Biologist 2 argues that finches' beaks grew larger because individual birds used their beaks more during the drought to crack hard seeds (acquired characteristic). Which observation would support Biologist 1 and refute Biologist 2?
options: The beak size of individual finches did not change during their lifetimes, but the average beak size of the population increased across generations
All finches on the island developed larger beaks within a single year
Finches with small beaks also survived the drought
Beak size is determined entirely by diet
questions.explanation: Natural selection (Biologist 1) predicts changes across generations via differential survival and reproduction, not within an individual's lifetime. If individual beak sizes didn't change but the population average increased over generations, that supports selection rather than acquired characteristics.

questions.stem: A chemist wants to test how temperature affects the rate of a chemical reaction. She runs the reaction at 20°C, 30°C, 40°C, and 50°C, measuring the time to completion at each temperature. To ensure reliable results, what should she do?
options: Repeat the reaction at each temperature multiple times and average the results
Change the amount of reactants at each temperature
Use a different reaction at each temperature
Run the reaction only once at each temperature
questions.explanation: Repeating trials at each temperature and averaging reduces the impact of random errors and improves the reliability of the data. Keeping other variables constant is also essential.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem: A graph shows the speed of an object over 10 seconds. The speed increases from 0 to 20 m/s during the first 4 seconds, stays at 20 m/s from 4 to 7 seconds, then decreases from 20 m/s to 0 m/s from 7 to 10 seconds. Which statement about the object's motion is correct?
options: The object accelerates for the first 4 seconds, moves at constant speed for 3 seconds, then decelerates for 3 seconds
The object moves at constant speed the entire time
The object accelerates throughout the 10 seconds
The object decelerates for the first 4 seconds
questions.explanation: The graph has three phases: acceleration (speed increasing, 0-4 s), constant speed (4-7 s), and deceleration (speed decreasing, 7-10 s). This matches the description in option A.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Average temperature (°C) and rainfall (mm) for four cities:
City: A | B | C | D
Temperature (°C): 28 | 15 | 10 | 22
Rainfall (mm): 1200 | 800 | 400 | 1500
Which city has the highest rainfall?
questions.explanation: City D has 1500 mm of rainfall, which is the highest value in the rainfall row.

questions.stem: A student tests the rate of rusting of iron nails in three environments: dry air, moist air, and water with salt. After two weeks, she observes that the nail in salt water rusted most, the nail in moist air rusted moderately, and the nail in dry air showed almost no rust. What conclusion is best supported?
options: Rusting requires both water and oxygen, and salt accelerates the process
Dry air causes the most rusting
Rusting occurs only in pure water
questions.explanation: The results show moisture is needed for rust (dry air: almost none), and salt water speeds rusting compared to moist air alone. This supports that rusting requires water and oxygen, with salt as an accelerator.

questions.stem: Two psychologists offer explanations for why people conform to group opinions. Psychologist 1 argues conformity results from informational influence: people genuinely change their views because they believe the group has better information. Psychologist 2 argues conformity results from normative influence: people publicly agree to gain acceptance, even while privately disagreeing. In a famous experiment, participants gave the same wrong answer as a group of actors about the length of a line. If participants privately believed their own answer but publicly agreed with the group, this would support:
options: Psychologist 1, because participants changed their genuine beliefs
Psychologist 2, because participants conformed publicly without changing their private beliefs
questions.explanation: Public agreement with private disagreement is the hallmark of normative influence described by Psychologist 2. Informational influence (Psychologist 1) would involve genuinely changing one's private belief.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the number of books read by four students in a month: Ana read 5, Ben read 8, Cara read 3, and Dan read 6. Who read the fewest books?
questions.explanation: Cara read 3 books, the fewest of the four students. Ben read the most (8).

questions.stem: Researchers test whether music affects plant growth. They play classical music to one group of plants, rock music to a second group, and no music to a third group. All plants receive identical water, light, and soil. Which statement about this experiment is correct?
options: The music type is the dependent variable
The group with no music serves as the control condition
Plant growth is the independent variable
The experiment cannot have a control group
questions.explanation: The no-music group is the control condition because it lacks the treatment (music). Plant growth is the dependent variable, and music type is the independent variable.

questions.stem: Two astronomers explain the observed redshift of light from distant galaxies. Astronomer 1 argues the redshift means the universe is expanding, so galaxies are moving away from each other. Astronomer 2 argues the light could be 'tired' — losing energy over its long journey, which would also produce redshift without expansion. Which observation would distinguish between the two hypotheses?
options: Redshift increases with distance in a consistent pattern that matches the predictions of expansion
Redshift is observed only in nearby galaxies
questions.explanation: Expansion predicts a specific relationship: the farther the galaxy, the greater the redshift (Hubble's law). A 'tired light' hypothesis would not produce this consistent distance-redshift relation. This pattern is key evidence distinguishing expansion from tired light.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Concentration of a pollutant (mg/L) in a river at increasing distance downstream from a factory:
Distance (km): 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8
Pollutant (mg/L): 50 | 42 | 30 | 15 | 5
What is the best explanation for the observed trend?
options: The pollutant is being diluted and/or broken down as it travels downstream
The factory releases more pollutant downstream
questions.explanation: Concentration decreases steadily with distance from the factory (50 to 5 mg/L), consistent with dilution by river water and natural degradation or settling of the pollutant.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
A graph shows the melting time of ice cubes (minutes) at different temperatures (°C):
Temperature: 0 | 10 | 20 | 30
Melting time (min): 45 | 30 | 20 | 12
How long does it take an ice cube to melt at 30°C?
questions.explanation: At 30°C, the ice cube melts in 12 minutes, according to the graph data.

questions.stem: Two theories explain why some animals hibernate. Theory 1: Hibernation is an adaptation to conserve energy when food is scarce during winter. Theory 2: Hibernation is triggered by cold temperatures alone, regardless of food availability. Which experimental observation would support Theory 1 over Theory 2?
options: Ground squirrels in a warm laboratory with abundant food do not hibernate, even in winter
Ground squirrels kept in the cold with plenty of food still hibernate
Hibernation occurs only in tropical species
Body temperature during hibernation drops to near freezing
questions.explanation: If hibernation is an energy-conserving adaptation to food scarcity (Theory 1), animals with abundant food would not hibernate even in winter. This directly supports Theory 1. Observation B would support the cold-trigger theory.

questions.stem: A medical researcher tests a new vaccine. She vaccinates 5,000 volunteers and gives a placebo to 5,000 others. Over the following year, 12 vaccinated participants contract the disease while 80 placebo participants do. Before concluding the vaccine is effective, what additional check is most important?
options: Confirming the difference is statistically significant (unlikely to be due to chance)
Ensuring the vaccinated group received larger doses
Discarding the results because some vaccinated people got sick
Testing the vaccine only on participants who were already immune
questions.explanation: With large samples, small differences can arise by chance. Statistical significance testing determines whether the 12 vs. 80 difference is real rather than random, which is essential before drawing conclusions.

questions.topic: Data representation — interpreting graphs and tables
questions.stem:
Table: Sound intensity (decibels, dB) recorded at increasing distance from a speaker:
Distance (m): 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16
Intensity (dB): 90 | 84 | 78 | 72 | 66
Which statement best describes the relationship between distance and sound intensity in this table?
options: Each doubling of distance reduces sound intensity by a constant 6 dB
Sound intensity decreases by half for every meter
Sound intensity is unrelated to distance
questions.explanation: Going from 1→2 m: 90→84 (down 6). 2→4 m: 84→78 (down 6). 4→8 m: 78→72 (down 6). Each doubling of distance lowers intensity by exactly 6 dB, a constant logarithmic relationship.

questions.stem: A marine biologist studies whether coral bleaching is caused by rising water temperature. She records the temperature and bleaching status of corals at 20 reef sites over 5 years. She finds that bleaching events occur almost exclusively in years when water temperature exceeds 30°C. What is the main limitation of drawing a causal conclusion from this study?
options: Correlation alone does not prove causation; other factors could also contribute to bleaching
The study lasted too many years
Coral reefs cannot be studied scientifically
Water temperature cannot be measured accurately
questions.explanation: Observational data can show correlation (bleaching co-occurs with high temperature) but cannot rule out other contributing factors (pollution, ocean acidification, disease). A controlled experiment would be needed for stronger causal evidence.

questions.stem: Two linguists debate why human language emerged. Linguist 1 argues language evolved gradually from simpler communication systems shared with other primates, developing over hundreds of thousands of years. Linguist 2 argues language appeared relatively suddenly, as a unique human capacity requiring a specific genetic or cognitive change. Which evidence would most strongly support Linguist 1's gradualist view?
options: Fossil evidence and comparative studies showing a continuous series of intermediate communication abilities across hominins and other primates
The fact that no other animal species uses language
Evidence that all human languages share the same grammatical structure
The discovery that language use requires no brain development
questions.explanation: Gradual evolution predicts intermediate stages in communication abilities across related species and over time. A continuous series of intermediate forms supports Linguist 1, while the absence of such intermediates would support a sudden origin (Linguist 2).
